title: Medical Requirements
description: Covers medical standards for drivers, including requirements for glasses/lenses, medication procedures, drug screening, and medical frequency.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What are the requirements for wearing glasses, contact lenses, and sunglasses?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Must have a spare pair of glasses if required. Sunglasses must be railway approved. Contact lenses must be suitable for the maximum turn of duty.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Only one pair of glasses is needed if they are shatterproof.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Any type of sunglasses is permitted as long as they reduce glare.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Contact lenses are not permitted for safety-critical roles.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Vision standards require drivers who need glasses to carry a spare pair. Any sunglasses worn must meet railway approval standards (often related to tint/category). Contact lenses are allowed but must be suitable for wearing throughout the entire shift duration.

knowledgeUnits.concept: What is the procedure when required to take prescribed or over-the-counter medicine?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Show medication advice card to pharmacist/doctor, state safety-critical role, ask about side effects/policy breach. Inform depot manager ASAP about prescribed drugs for Medigold check. Report before duty, not at sign-on.
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Only report medication if it explicitly states 'may cause drowsiness'.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Inform the depot manager only if you feel side effects after taking the medicine.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Over-the-counter medicine does not need to be reported.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: When taking any medication, drivers must check with the prescriber/pharmacist about suitability for their safety-critical role. Crucially, prescribed medication must be reported to the depot manager immediately (before duty) so occupational health (Medigold) can assess fitness to work.

knowledgeUnits.concept: Why would you be asked to undergo drug screening?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Random (part of a percentage testing program), For Cause (after an incident), or Behavioural (suspicion of being under the influence).
knowledgeUnits.distractor1: Only required annually as part of the medical.
knowledgeUnits.distractor2: Only if involved in a major accident causing injury.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Drug screening can be requested for three main reasons: randomly as part of company policy, 'for cause' following a safety incident to rule out influence, or due to specific behavioural concerns indicating potential impairment.

knowledgeUnits.concept: How often would you be required to attend a medical?
knowledgeUnits.definition: Up to 55 years: every 3 years. Over 55 years: every year.
knowledgeUnits.distractor3: Every 3 years up to age 60, then annually.
knowledgeUnits.explanation: Periodic medical examinations are required to ensure ongoing fitness. The frequency increases with age: drivers attend every 3 years up to age 55, and then annually thereafter.
